doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Trombonists, old string bands and dance steps
title: What colored dancers danced: waltz, schottische, slow drag, cakewalk
summary: Colored dancers did the waltz, schottische, two-step, slow drag and cakewalk, often for prizes until midnight. Martin says bands then played from midnight to four in the alley-type places.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: They danced only the quadrilles. What did the color people dance? Mostly those, what kind of time or what kind of...
Dance, the waltz. Waltz. Shardas. Shardas. And, uh, two steps. Two steps.
What about the slow drag? You know, our friend's slow drag, Papajal, you used to win contests, he says, in the slow drags.
Yeah. You see, then they had, uh, kink walk. Kink walk, that's right. Kink walk.
Kink walk. Kink walk, that's right. Is that sort of like ragtime or what would it be like?

Yeah, no, that's slow. Yeah, slow. Fella walked a kick, you know what I mean? See, they used to... They used to... Yeah. They used to dance them, uh, uh, like they danced now. They used to have a fella who used to do that too, like, uh, that boy dance.

Like the tap dancing? Yeah, yeah. You see, uh, they used to give dance at that time from eight to four. Yeah. Yeah. All right, now you take from eight to twelve, well, that's what went on. See, the waltz, the shardas, the card drill, cake walk. Well, that went on. Well, now they used to dance that for prize. That's right. Up until midnight. Midnight, that's the midnight.
Midnight, well, now the band... You see, we turn them loose then.

We go in and play in the alley. We say we go in the alley. We go in the alley. Yeah. Yeah, yeah. After the alley. They put them in the alley. Yeah. But now all them... The old rag... Them, uh, ladies with their good daughters and things, well, they gone. They gone. Yeah. They gone. Well, they all get full of them... With the rats. You know what? That's from twelve to four.
stuff Well, in them times, why this was different than today.
